recipes.name: Curried Chicken
ingredients_raw: 1 whole chicken, cut into 8 pieces and skin removed
salt and ground black pepper to taste
1 tablespoon curry powder, or more to taste
1 (10.75 ounce) can cream of mushroom soup

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Arrange chicken pieces in a single layer in a 9x13-inch baking dish. Season chicken liberally with salt, pepper, and paprika; set aside.

Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add apple and onion to hot butter, season with curry powder, and cook and stir until apple and onion are tender, 7 to 10 minutes. Stir in condensed soup and half-and-half until completely combined; spoon over chicken pieces in the baking dish.

Bake in the preheated oven until chicken is no longer pink at the bone and the juices run clear, about 75 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the thigh, near the bone, should read 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Curried Chicken
raw_recipe.description: This is a very easy and delicious curried chicken recipe that uses cream of mushroom soup and half-and-half cream to make a delectable sauce.

review.reviewBody: I wanted to make it a bit more healthy so I only used boneless, skinless, chicken breast. I cut them up into chunks and cooked them in a wok with the onions, apples, paprika, salt, pepper, and butter. I also used skim milk instead of cream. This was really good, and time saving. I just didn't have 2 hours to make dinner. I would also suggest putting a crunchy green veg. in there as well, maybe sugar snap peas. I served it over long grain brown rice. The sauce was amazing though, and the recipe was really easy to convert. I loved making it a one dish sort of dish, aside from the rice.

I loved it, I used chicken breast, added 1 clove garlic, couple of stalks of celery, and a small pepper cut up. I did it on the stove top because it was too hot to put the oven on. I browned all the vegies first, made the sauce, put in a bowl while I browned the chicken, then added vegies back and cooked on the stove for about 1/2 hour! I used cream of celery soup because my husband doesn't like mushrooms.

I used two large boneless, skinless chicken breasts, diced. Sauteed them in the butter with the onion & apple. Mixed the other ingredients, together (added 1 tsp chili powder). Then thickened the sauce a bit in my instant pot using the saute' function. Added chicken mixture and set to manual pressure for 5 min. Quick release. Served over rice. Big hit!! Yum!!

So I followed the recipe for the most part but used boneless skinless chicken breast instead, sautéed the apple and onion with olive oil for about 5mins then added chicken chunks with salt and pepper to taste... in a separate bowl I mixed the paprika/curry powder/ mush soup and used sweetened coconut milk instead of half and half. Once the chicken was cooked I added the sauce and perfecto!!! I let the sauce boil and then simmered for about 10-15mins...

I make it gluten free with homemade gluten free chicken soup (3/4 cup organic chicken stock, 3/4 cup milk and 3 TBL gluten free cornstarch) and still add 1 cup half-and-half cream. I love curry powder and add turmeric also. Cut chicken into smaller chunks so cooking lasts

So easy to make! I decided to make it on the stove top since i didnt have a lot of time. i added peas ( a nice suggestion from someone) and i used 1 % milk because that was what i had. i thought two tablespoons of curry helped cover up a bit of the cream of mushroom taste, but the combo really was delicious! Next time i think ill add mushrooms! :) Definitely adding this to the rotation!

I've made this a million times now and it's a big hit with my family. My husband LOVES every time I make this. The small changes I make is chicken breasts cooked and sautéed in a large skillet. It's completely unnecessary to cook a whole chicken in the oven - in my opinion. Also, for a healthier option, I use coconut milk instead of heavy cream. If I need to thicken the sauce a bit, I'll mix some cold water with corn starch and add it into the sauce. This recipe is fantastic. Give it a try. Oh, and I recommend granny smith apples for the best flavor. Edit 2/6/24: I just wanted to come back and say that this recipe is still a constant rotation in my household. Sometimes I feel like going the heavy cream route, and it is still as delicious as ever. Make sure you always sauté the onions and apples first in oil along with the spices, or the apples will remain crispy and not soften. I have used cream of chicken when I didn't have mushroom, and it was not a problem. And I still only add cubes of chicken breast (don't forget to salt them) into the apples/onion mix. Such an easy and flavorful weeknight meal.

We love this dish; it is a household favorite. The kids (all twelve and under) actually cheer when they learn this is planned for dinner! I make it all in one pan for simplicity and use boneless skinless chicken thighs due to preference. It can be done entirely stovetop. Served with rice. Not sure if it authentic, but it is yummy. The apples are a nice touch. Sometimes we add golden raisins.

This recipe is a great start, and tasty, but I used far more spices. Here's what I added, FWIW: I added a fresh, diced long hot pepper and a diced poblano pepper, and a teaspoon of minced garlic to the onion, apple, and butter sauté. I doubled the curry and mushroom soup, and I added 2 Tbsp minced ginger, 1 Tbsp garlic powder, 1 Tbsp brown sugar, 1 Tbsp tomato paste, and 1 Tbsp cayenne to the sauce. I sprinkled smoked paprika, salt, black and cayenne pepper, and garlic on both sides of the skinless, boneless chicken (and I cooked it only 45 minutes (no bones!). I also added a cup of fresh green beans and an already baked sweet potato (just because it was in the fridge (and it was yummy). So, I can only imagine that cooked as is it would not have been nearly spicy enough of a curry for me. However my alterations brought the spice level up to my standards.

Easy and delicious. Like another cook, I also wanted it faster so I browned the chicken in a pan then added everything else and cooked till veggies were tender. So simple. i added mushrooms, green pepper, frozen corn and a bit of maple syrup to sweeten. Mixed milk with cream to lessen fat. Served over rice. Everyone loved it.

Great base! Made this for my mom, who is pescatarian, and used eggplant, zucchini, onion, and mushrooms. I did it as a stir fry instead of baking it, obviously. Also added a tsp of garlic and used coconut cream instead of half and half.

Really good! It was interesting to try a curry that isn't tied to a particular ethnic cuisine such as Indian or Thai. I made this using boneless chicken thighs and Campbell's Cream of Cremini & Shiitake Mushroom soup. Served with couscous and poured the extra sauce over the chicken and couscous. I don't really think it needs anything else, but I might try adding another apple and also serving with some sauteed mushrooms. For a spicy version, I might try serving with half regular paprika and half hot Hungarian paprika.
No changes were made. Absolutely delicious!
It’s a different twist of chicken curry. ??

This was an absolutely delicious recipe! I followed the advice that someone left in a comment to throw everything together in a skillet to save time, and it turned out perfectly! I cooked the apples and onions with the butter and curry powder in the skillet first, while I seasoned cubed chicken breasts in a bowl with paprika, salt, and pepper. I added the chicken to the apples and onions in the skillet, and after the chicken was cooked I threw in the mushroom soup mixed with cream. I will be making this again and again!
My husband and daughter love this recipe! I have been making it on a weekly basis.
Fantastic! The only change I made was to use skim milk instead of half and half. Great combination of flavors. Served over brown rice. Will definitely make again.
This recipe was delish! Followed it per directions, except I had boneless skinless thighs so I used them instead of a whole chicken. Family LOVED it! Am cooking this again soon!
Tired out great
Very good ! Me and my family loved this
